Frozen Bear Creek

memories below

Powder Hush

Snow turns the volume down. Evergreen is a short drive west of Denver, but a little way up Bear Creek it feels like another world: a deep blue sky, a packed trail winding between pine and fir, and a creek hushed under its ice. The snow was soft and deep, and by midday the sun was throwing long blue shadows across every drift. In winter, bring traction. A trail this well trodden turns to ice in a hurry.

The trail stayed close to the creek, and the rock was the main attraction. Boulders stacked on the bank, granite I think, wore thick caps of snow, their faces streaked with what looked like orange lichen. The dog in the blue jacket had other priorities. It sprinted ahead until it was a speck between the trees, doubled back at full speed, then flopped into powder and rolled over completely, as if snow angels were serious business.

Further along, the trail edged out onto a ledge. I looked down through the pine boughs into a cleft of rock packed full of snow and stood there a while. It doesn't take a fourteener to feel small. A frozen creek and a pile of old granite will do just fine. Then I retraced the footprints back out, already hoping to return when the ice lets go and I can hear what this creek actually sounds like.
